name: standard-v2
note: CALIBRATED 2026-09-06 AND FAILED. DO NOT USE. Three runs, 179 decided games, subjects edgar-vampires / ur-dragon / zur-enchantress: nekusar-discard took 0.637 [0.564, 0.704], 2.55x fair, DOMINATES. That is WORSE than the giada-angels 0.597 this table was built to escape. abaddon 0.151 (0.6x), muldrotha-value 0.056 (0.22x, floor), and the subject null is 0.151 — the same 0.6x the old table gave, so nothing was gained. THE ERROR IS RECORDED BECAUSE IT WAS AVOIDABLE: this file's previous note already said nekusar's 0.273 was measured in a FIVE-player pod and does not transfer, and the seat was chosen on that number anyway. A cross-table share is not a power ranking. A HYPOTHESIS WAS TESTED AND REFUTED HERE, which is the part worth keeping. The table is four grindy value decks with no clock — 58 of 59 games in the first run ended 'all opponents have lost' rather than by a kill — so the reading was that a deck winning without combat wins by default and that pressure would suppress it. It does not. nekusar scored 0.661 / 0.617 / 0.633 against a control deck, an AGGRO deck and a big-mana deck, a spread of 0.044 across three very different subjects. edgar-vampires did reach 0.233 against 0.085 for zur, but it took that from abaddon (0.186 -> 0.100) and muldrotha (0.068 -> 0.033), NOT from nekusar. Symmetric non-combat damage hits three opponents at once and does not care what the board looks like. WHAT A THIRD TABLE NEEDS: of thirteen opponent seats ever measured, only abaddon (0.76x) and jarad-graveyard (0.77x) land near fair; five dominate above 1.69x and six are floors below 0.4x. Picking three from that pool by pooled share would repeat this mistake, because a pooled share is confounded by whoever else sat at the table. The measurement that has never been made is a ROUND ROBIN AMONG CANDIDATE OPPONENTS WITH NONE OF OUR DECKS SEATED — that ranks them on a level field instead of inferring strength from tables they happened to sit at.

seats.note: Kept. 0.217 [0.174, 0.268] over 290 decided games in `standard`, 0.87x fair — the only seat any table has produced that sits near even.
1.36x fair in the FIVE-player playgroup pod, the middle band there. Non-combat damage is the axis PRD-v1 s14 says actually wins, and the old standard table had none of it.
UNMEASURED anywhere. Here for the axis rather than for a number: a value chain that survives wipes, which is the other half of the s14 note.
